land.text: the Silesian Province of Bolesław III's testament, held with the Seniorate by Władysław II until 1146

predecessors.note: The page gives 'Established: 1138' as a province of Poland; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1138.

land.text: Cliopatria's Legnica shape covers Wrocław in 1305-1313

successors.note: The Silesia page runs the Wrocław duchy of Henry VI the Good to 1335 (1327 inheritance treaty with John of Bohemia; Treaty of Trentschin 1335); this dossier stops at Cliopatria's last Silesia shape (1304), after which Cliopatria shows Wrocław inside its Duchy of Legnica row (1305-1313).

land.text: Cliopatria's Bohemian shape covers Wrocław from 1314

successors.note: Page: 1327 the remaining Duchy of Wrocław passed under Bohemian suzerainty; 1335 Casimir III renounced Silesia and Henry VI's duchy passed to Bohemia; 1348 Treaty of Namysłów.

capitals.name: Wrocław (Breslau)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Wrocław (51°6′N 17°1′E)'; Głogów, Legnica, Opole, Racibórz and later duchies were partitions with their own seats.

rulers.name: Władysław II the Exile
rulers.note: Senior duke of Poland and duke of Silesia; exiled in 1146.

rulers.name: Bolesław IV the Curly
rulers.title: High Duke holding Silesia
rulers.note: 'took control' in 1146; Barbarossa's 1157 expedition forced him to cede Silesia; the sons returned in 1163.

rulers.name: Bolesław I the Tall
rulers.note: With Mieszko Tanglefoot at first (retook the main cities in 1165); died 7 or 8 December 1201.

rulers.name: Henry I the Bearded
rulers.note: High Duke of Poland from 1232; died 19 March 1238.

rulers.name: Henry III the White
rulers.note: Ruled jointly with his brother Władysław (1248-1270, Archbishop of Salzburg); died 3 December 1266.

rulers.name: Henry IV Probus
rulers.note: Minor to 1273 (Henry IV page: 'formally proclaimed an adult' in 1273); High Duke of Poland from 1288/89; died 23 June 1290.

rulers.name: Henry VI the Good
rulers.note: Ruled to 1335 on the page; the dossier stops at 1304.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1139 shape applied one year earlier: the Silesian Province of Władysław II

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1139, the page gives 'Established: 1138'. The page has no infobox area (the Wrocław article name redirects to this page), so the area comparison was not possible.

1139-1146, 121,796 km2 (514 cells): the lands of Władysław II. The testament gives him the Seniorate Province (western Lesser Poland, eastern Greater Poland, western Kuyavia, Wieluń Land and Kraków), the Silesian Province and the Łęczyca and Sieradz Lands (held for life by Salomea), and the senior's control over the vassals in Pomerelia; the shape holds all of these and a margin of eastern Kuyavia and Masovia (Bolesław IV's Masovian Province), within the precision of the era. The Silesian core alone is the 1169 shape.

correction.text: Lower Silesia with Lubusz Land (the 1169 Silesia shape) and Upper Silesia (the 1169 Wrocław-row shape), ruled jointly by Bolesław I and Mieszko Tanglefoot

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1163-1168, a period Cliopatria draws inside the Duchy of Masovia's big shape (166,473 km2). 'In 1163, Władysław's sons returned to the duchy and ruled jointly at Wrocław' (Testament page: 'his sons managed to retain the Silesian Province in 1163, losing the Seniorate'). Upper Silesia is still part of the duchy: the partition came in 1172 (infobox) or 1173 (Bolesław I page). The Masovia dossier should drop Silesia from its 1147-1168 shape.

1169-1176, 28,682 km2: Wrocław, Legnica, Głogów, Złotoryja and the Lubusz Land to the Oder (gazetteer check: it holds Kłodzko, Wałbrzych and Zielona Góra). Bolesław I the Tall 'Duke of Wrocław from 1163 until his death in 1201'; Silesia page: first partition 1172. The page is silent on Lubusz before 1206 (planned swap for Kalisz), so the Lubusz part is unverified (confidence 1).

correction.text: Lower Silesia and Lubusz without the Głogów lands of Konrad Spindleshanks (radius 45 km assumed)

keyframe_review.note: 1177-1187, 28,768 km2: as 1169 without the Głogów lands, which Bolesław 'was compelled to give ... to his youngest brother Konrad' after returning to his duchy in 1177 by Casimir II's mediation (Silesia page: 'Głogów split off: 1177'). Reintegration is dated 1190 on the Bolesław I page (Konrad's death without issue) and 'c. 1185' in the Silesia infobox, which also says 'Głogów and Opole fell back to Bolesław I' in 1190 and 1201.

correction.text: The Silesian core without Głogów to 1189, whole from 1190

keyframe_review.note: 1188-1201, 29,008 km2: as 1177 until 1190 (Głogów with Konrad), whole after Konrad's death 'without issue in 1190' (ledger). Bolesław obtained a protective bull from Innocent III in 1198; he inherited Opole on Jarosław's death (22 March 1201, ledger) and died on 7 or 8 December 1201.

correction.text: The Silesian core without Opole: Henry I the Bearded's duchy after Mieszko Tanglefoot took Opole in early 1202

keyframe_review.note: 1202-1205, 34,715 km2: the 1201 realm with Opole (90% of the Opole voivodeship) and Bytom. 'Early 1202: His uncle, Mieszko IV Tanglefoot, took the Duchy of Opole from Henry's possession', so Opole is not Henry's from 1202; the shape Cliopatria itself draws from 1206 (29,075 km2) is the Silesian core without it and is used for 1202-1205. Henry I became duke at Wrocław in 1201.

1206-1209, 29,075 km2: the core of Henry I. 1206: Władysław III Spindleshanks was deposed at Kraków; the planned swap of Lubusz for Kalisz was foiled (Silesia page); in 1208 Henry and Władysław III met at Głogów after Henry had given Kalisz (except Poznań) to Władysław Odonic. Kalisz is outside the outline.

1210-1219, 29,031 km2: the core of Henry I with Lubusz. On 6 May 1210 Margrave Konrad II of Lusatia died and Henry took Lubusz and Gubin, which he held until 1218 (page); the Silesia page says Henry 'regained' Lubusz in 1210. Henry lost Lubusz in 1218 (ledger, confidence 1) and the outline of 1220-1235 is corrected to match; for 1169-1209 Cliopatria already holds Lubusz in the Silesian outline although the Henry I page has Henry 'take' it in 1210 (confidence 1 for the earlier years).

correction.text: The Silesian core without Lubusz Land, which Henry did not hold between 1218 and 1229-1230

keyframe_review.note: 1220-1226, 29,075 km2: as 1206 without Lubusz. Henry took Lubusz and Gubin in 1210 and 'held [them] until 1218'; he 'added Lubusz to his duchy' only in 1229-1230 (page). In between Landgrave Louis IV of Thuringia 'began campaigns against Lubusz' in 1221 (Silesia page) and in 1225 Henry withdrew from Kraków when Louis IV attacked Lubusz; the page names no holder 1218-1229 (ledger loss at confidence 1).

correction.text: The Silesian core of Henry I without Lubusz Land until 1229-1230

keyframe_review.note: 1227-1235, 28,920 km2: Henry I's Silesia, the core, without Lubusz until 1229-1230 (ledger gain; the page has Henry Raspe resign his rights in 1229 and Henry add Lubusz to his duchy). The seniorate (Kraków, 116,822 km2) is drawn by Cliopatria under the Duchy of Greater Poland in these years, though Henry the Bearded was made governor of Kraków at Cienia (5 May 1228) and entered Kraków as High Duke in 1232; his lands grew by Lubusz (1230), Kraków (1232), half of Greater Poland up to the Warta (summer 1234) and Opole (1234): ledger events.

correction.text: Silesia, Kraków and Lesser Poland, Greater Poland (Poznań, Kalisz, Gniezno) and, to 1239, the Opole regency under Henry II the Pious

keyframe_review.note: 1236-1240, 120,098 km2 (514 cells: Kuyavia 77%, Pomerelia 63%, Masovia 33% of those regions). 'When Henry the Bearded died on 19 March 1238, Henry the Pious became duke of Silesia, Kraków and Greater Poland'; he took most of Władysław Odonic's lands, including Gniezno, after Odonic's death on 5 June 1239, and held 'Duke of Greater Poland (Only in the Southwest) 1238-1241' (infobox). Nothing on the pages puts Kuyavia, Pomerelia or Masovia in his hands; the corrected shape is Silesia, Lesser Poland, Greater Poland and Opole (the Opole regency ended in 1239).

correction.text: The Silesian core (Wrocław, Legnica, Głogów, Lubusz) held by Henry II's sons under regency from 1241

keyframe_review.note: 1241-1249, 110,720 km2: Cliopatria keeps the 1236-1240 realm after Henry II's death on 9 April 1241, but the pages say Henry's 'lands at death' were Silesia, Wrocław and southwestern Greater Poland and that Kraków was lost: Konrad of Masovia entered Kraków on 10 July 1241 and Bolesław V of Sandomierz regained it on 25 May 1243. The corrected shape is the Silesian core: Wrocław, Legnica, Głogów and Lubusz under Bolesław II the Bald (Lubusz granted to Mieszko in 1241 and regained in 1242), until the 1248 division.

1250-1278, 12,797 km2: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry III the White (Wrocław and Wałbrzych in the outline) after the 1248 division in which 'Bolesław II chose Legnica, and Henry received Wrocław'; Głogów went to Konrad (1250-1251) and Lubusz was sold off by Bolesław II. In 1253-1254 'the Duchy of Wrocław was besieged and plundered' after Henry repudiated his treaty with Przemysł I and Bolesław the Pious; in 1270 King Ottokar II of Bohemia 'also took over Wrocław' after Władysław's death (Henry IV page).

correction.text: The Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus without the one-third that he gave Bolesław II of Legnica in 1277-78 (Środa Śląska and Strzegom)

keyframe_review.note: 1279-1293, 19,123 km2 (94 cells; the outline gains Zielona Góra and Lubusz, 12.8 to 19.1 thousand km2, with no page behind the growth). Henry IV Probus ruled the Duchy of Wrocław in his own right from 1273; to pay his ransom at the end of 1277-78 he gave Bolesław II 'one-third of his duchy, including Środa Śląska and Strzegom' and pledged Krosno Odrzańskie; 'Henry also seized Kalisz' in 1284 and traded it for Ołobok; he took Kraków in August 1289 and died on 23 June 1290. The ransom land is cut from the outline.

correction.text: The Wrocław duchy of Henry VI the Good without the Świdnica towns (to Jawor) and the 1277-78 ransom lands

keyframe_review.note: 1294-1304, 19,123 km2 (same outline as 1279). 'The duchy lost its southern territories in 1290-1291': Kłodzko Land passed to Bohemia and 'the towns of Świdnica, Dzierżoniów, Ząbkowice, Ziębice and Strzelin passed to Jawor' (Cliopatria has its own Duchy of Jawor shape of 3,584 km2 from 1279); in 1296 Henry V's heritage was divided among his sons and Henry VI the Good ruled the duchy from 1296 (page list). The corrected shape cuts the Świdnica lands and the 1277-78 ransom lands from the outline.

correction.text: Upper Silesia (Opole, Racibórz, Bytom) as the Silesian Piast lands of the undivided duchy until 1171, then the duchies of Racibórz and Opole

keyframe_review.note: 1169-1176, 12,555 km2 (52 cells, 96% inside the Upper Silesia region; the outline holds Opole, Racibórz and Bytom): Cliopatria's 'Duchy of Wrocław' row lies on Upper Silesia, not on Wrocław (Lower Silesia is the Duchy of Silesia row above). The Silesia page treats Wrocław as the same state (the 'Duchy of Wrocław' title is an alias) and has Upper Silesia inside it until the partition of 1172 (Racibórz to Mieszko I, a strip around Opole to Jarosław; Bolesław I page: 1173). So the shape is Silesian for 1169-1171 and then Mieszko's and Jarosław's duchies (ledger 'split' events in 1172).

correction.text: Use the Duchy of Silesia shape (Lower Silesia and Lubusz); Opole, Racibórz and Bytom are other duchies from 1172

keyframe_review.note: 1177-1191, 5,861 km2 (25 cells; Opole and Bytom, not Racibórz). The shape is not the Duchy of Wrocław: after 1172 Wrocław is the Lower Silesian duchy of Bolesław I (the Duchy of Silesia row), and the Upper Silesian land is Jarosław's Opole (Cliopatria's Duchy of Opole row has its own 6,536 km2 shape on top of this one from 1177) and Mieszko Tanglefoot's Racibórz, to which Casimir II granted 'the Lesser Polish districts of Bytom, Oświęcim and Pszczyna' (c. 1177). Use the Duchy of Silesia shape for the Wrocław duchy; the Upper Silesian duchies need their own dossiers.

correction.text: Use the Duchy of Silesia shape (Lower Silesia and Lubusz); Opole joins it only from March 1201 to early 1202

keyframe_review.note: 1192-1201, 5,861 km2: as 1177. Jarosław of Opole died on 22 March 1201 and Bolesław I 'inherited Opole, which was again reunited with his lands' (ledger gain), lost to Mieszko in early 1202.

region.text: the Silesian Province (Oder basin between the Sudetes and Greater Poland), with the Seniorate lands of Władysław II

ledger.note: 1138: the Silesian Province is formed under Władysław II. 'Soon after it was formed under the Piast dynasty in 1138, it fragmented into various Silesian duchies'; infobox 'Established: 1138', 'Status: Province of Poland'. The testament gave Władysław II 'the Silesian Province' with the Seniorate (Testament page). The page gives the Oder basin as the territory, not a boundary.

region.text: Silesia and the Seniorate lands of Władysław II

ledger.note: 1146: Władysław II is exiled and Silesia goes to Bolesław IV. 'Władysław lost senior status and fled to the Holy Roman Empire; Bolesław IV the Curly took control.' The Silesia dossier has no territory 1147-1162 (Cliopatria draws it inside the Duchy of Masovia's shape).

region.text: Silesia from Lubusz to Upper Silesia, the Silesian Province of the testament

ledger.note: 1163: Władysław's sons return to Wrocław. 'In 1163, Władysław's sons returned to the duchy and ruled jointly at Wrocław'; Testament page: 'his sons managed to retain the Silesian Province in 1163, losing the Seniorate'. Barbarossa's 1157 campaign 'forced Bolesław IV to cede Silesia' (Silesia page) and the Nuremberg agreement admitted the exiled princes (Bolesław I page).

region.text: Racibórz, the share of Mieszko I Tanglefoot

ledger.note: 1172: the brothers partition the duchy, Racibórz to Mieszko. Infobox 'Racibórz split off: 1172'; 'Brothers partitioned the duchy after open conflict; Mieszko I got Racibórz'. The Bolesław I page dates the division to Bolesław's return 'at the beginning of 1173' and the Duke of Silesia page's table has 'Opole-Racibórz (Upper Silesia) first created' in 1163 and the Duchy of Racibórz in 1173.

region.text: a strip around Opole, the share of Jarosław

ledger.note: 1172: a strip around Opole goes to Jarosław. Infobox 'Opole split off: 1172'; 'Jarosław got a strip around Opole'.

region.text: the Głogów lands of Konrad Spindleshanks

ledger.note: 1177: Bolesław returns by Casimir II's mediation and must give Głogów to his brother Konrad. 'he was compelled to give Głogów to his youngest brother Konrad'; infobox 'Głogów split off: 1177'.
1190: Głogów returns to Bolesław. 'His brother Konrad's death without issue in 1190 resulted in the return of Głogów to his domains.' The Silesia infobox has 'Głogów reintegrated: c. 1185'.

region.text: the Duchy of Opole of Jarosław

ledger.note: 1201: Opole is reunited with Silesia. 'after Jarosław's death on 22 March 1201, to inherit Opole, which was again reunited with his lands'.

Early 1202: Mieszko Tanglefoot takes Opole from Henry the Bearded. 'Early 1202: His uncle, Mieszko IV Tanglefoot, took the Duchy of Opole from Henry's possession.' Silesia page: 'Mieszko I annexed the Opole territory' in 1202.

ledger.counterpart: Konrad II of Lusatia (Margraviate of Lusatia)
ledger.note: 1210: Henry the Bearded takes Lubusz and Gubin. '6 May 1210: Margrave Konrad II of Lusatia died, and Henry took Lubusz and Gubin, which he held until 1218'; the Silesia page says Henry 'regained Lubusz after the margrave's death'.

1218: Lubusz is no longer Henry's. The Henry I page has him holding it 'until 1218' and names no holder; Landgrave Louis IV of Thuringia 'began campaigns against Lubusz' in 1221 and Henry Raspe resigned his Lubusz rights in 1229 (counterpart bridged from those two facts).

1229-1230: Henry takes Lubusz again. 'Henry Raspe resigned his Lubusz rights (1229) and sold his claim to Archbishop Albert (1230). Henry then added Lubusz to his duchy, without Władysław III's consent.' Henry II had led an expedition to secure Lubusz in 1229-1230 (Henry II page).

region.text: Sandomierz under Henry the Bearded's regency

ledger.note: 1231: Henry the Bearded takes over the regency of Sandomierz for the minor Bolesław V. 'Henry the Bearded took over Sandomierz after Grzymisława gave up the regency'; the Henry I page confirms him 'as regent of Sandomierz' in the 1233 Treaty of Chełm.

region.text: Kraków and Lesser Poland, the High Duke's seat

ledger.note: 1232: Henry the Bearded enters Kraków as High Duke. '1232: Henry entered Kraków and was proclaimed High Duke and overlord of Poland'; Cienia (5 May 1228) had made him only 'Governor of Kraków', and in 1229 Konrad of Masovia captured him at Spytkowice. Counterpart is Cliopatria's: its Greater Poland shape covers Kraków 1227-1235.

region.text: Greater Poland south of the Warta with Kalisz and Poznań

ledger.note: Summer 1234: Odonic gives Henry half of Greater Poland. 'Odonic agreed to give Henry the half of Greater Poland up to the Warta River, including Kalisz and Poznań. Henry II the Pious was installed there as duke.'
1234: Henry takes direct control of Opole. 'Henry took direct control of Opole' (as guardian of Casimir I of Opole's minor sons from 1230).
August 1234: the Treaty of Luchani gives Bolesław V Sandomierz. 'The Treaty of Luchani gave Bolesław Sandomierz'; Pope Gregory IX approved it in June 1235.
1238: Henry II the Pious is regent of Sandomierz and Opole-Racibórz. 'He served as regent of Sandomierz and Opole-Racibórz'; Henry the Bearded died on 19 March 1238.
1239: Henry II gives up the regency of Upper Silesia. 'Henry II gave up the regency of Upper Silesia to Mieszko II.'

5 June 1239: Władysław Odonic dies and Henry II takes his lands. 'The situation changed unexpectedly after the death of Władysław Odonic on 5 June 1239.' Henry took most of Odonic's lands, including Gniezno.

9 July 1239: Bolesław V takes over Sandomierz. 'On 9 July, at Przedbórz, Konrad renounced his claims to Sandomierz, and Bolesław began his personal government.' Henry II 'was compelled to resign the regency' in 1239 (Henry II page).

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Lubusz (Mieszko, son of Henry II)
ledger.note: 1241: Lubusz is granted to Mieszko. 'Lubusz was granted to Mieszko' after Henry II fell at Legnica. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: counterpart was duchy-of-opole; the Silesia page says Henry II's widow 'in 1241 granted it to his second son Mieszko' and Bolesław II 'regained Lubusz upon the death of his brother Mieszko in 1242'.]

region.text: Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno held in 1238-1241

ledger.note: 1241: Greater Poland is no longer Silesian. The page lists Henry II's lands at death as 'Silesia, the High Duke title, Wrocław, and southwestern Greater Poland'; none of the pages opened says who took them. The 1250 Cliopatria shape no longer holds them (bridge, confidence 1).

10 July 1241: Konrad of Masovia enters Kraków. After the Battle of Legnica (9 April) 'all of Lesser Poland, including Kraków and Sandomierz, fell under Mongol control' (Henry II page); 'On 10 July 1241 Konrad entered Kraków' and Bolesław V regained it on 25 May 1243.

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Lubusz (Mieszko, son of Henry II)
ledger.note: 1242: Lubusz is reintegrated. Infobox 'Lubusz reintegrated: 1242'; Bolesław II regained it after Mieszko's death. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: counterpart was duchy-of-opole; the Silesia page says Henry II's widow 'in 1241 granted it to his second son Mieszko' and Bolesław II 'regained Lubusz upon the death of his brother Mieszko in 1242'.]

region.text: the Legnica, Głogów and Lubusz districts of Bolesław II

ledger.note: 1248: Silesia is divided between the brothers. After a year of co-rule 'the brothers divided the Legnica, Głogów, Lubusz and Wrocław districts. Bolesław II chose Legnica, and Henry received Wrocław'; infobox 'Legnica split off: 1248'. The 12.8 thousand km2 Wrocław duchy of Cliopatria's 1250 shape is what is left. Głogów went to Konrad in 1250-1251 and Lubusz was sold by Bolesław II (to Brandenburg per the Silesia page, half to the Archbishop of Magdeburg per the Henry III page).

region.text: one-third of the duchy including Środa Śląska and Strzegom

ledger.note: End of 1277-78: Henry IV Probus pays his ransom in land. After being seized at Jelcz and defeated at Stolec (24 April 1277), Henry 'paid ransom by giving Bolesław II one-third of his duchy, including Środa Śląska and Strzegom' and pledged Krosno Odrzańskie. The page dates the payment 'end of year 1277-78'.

region.text: the Zielona Góra and Lubusz lands of the 1279 outline

ledger.note: 1279: Cliopatria's outline grows to Zielona Góra and the Lubusz Land. None of the pages opened explains this (Henry IV 'pledged Krosno Odrzańskie' in 1277-78, which shows he held land there). All 28 new cells (14.7-16.0 E, 51.5-52.4 N, and one at 16.9 E) lie inside Cliopatria's Duchy of Głogów shape of 1278 (gazetteer check), which is why that row is the counterpart. Bridge, confidence 1.

August 1289: Henry IV Probus takes Kraków. 'Henry regrouped his forces and marched against Kraków in person at the head of his army in August 1289.' He became High Duke after Leszek the Black's death (30 September 1288).
1290-1291: the duchy loses its southern territories. 'Kłodzko Land passed to Bohemia' (outside the 1279 outline).

region.text: the towns of Świdnica, Dzierżoniów, Ząbkowice, Ziębice and Strzelin

ledger.note: 1290-1291: the Świdnica towns pass to Jawor. 'the towns of Świdnica, Dzierżoniów, Ząbkowice, Ziębice and Strzelin passed to Jawor'; Cliopatria's Duchy of Jawor row starts in 1279.

23 June 1290: Henry IV dies and bequeaths Kraków to Przemysł II. 'he bequeathed the Duchy of Wrocław to Duke Henry III of Głogów, and Kraków [to Przemysł II]'; the death date 23 June is the best supported (others 24 June, 22 July, April).

region.text: the Wrocław duchy of Henry VI the Good

ledger.note: 1304: last year of the Cliopatria Silesia shape. The Wrocław duchy of Henry VI the Good lived on to 1335 (1327 inheritance treaty with John of Bohemia; at Trentschin in 1335 Casimir III renounced Silesia; Henry VI died three months later and his duchy passed to Bohemia; Treaty of Namysłów 1348), but Cliopatria draws Wrocław in its Duchy of Legnica row 1305-1313 and in Bohemia from 1314.

wars.name: Barbarossa's expedition against Poland (1157)
wars.outcome: Bolesław IV the Curly submitted to the emperor and was forced to cede Silesia; Władysław's sons returned in 1163 by the agreement signed at Nuremberg.
wars.note: The Silesia page: 'Frederick I Barbarossa campaigned in Greater Poland and forced Bolesław IV to cede Silesia'.

wars.name: Revolt of Mieszko Tanglefoot and the partition of 1172
wars.outcome: Mieszko Tanglefoot revolted in 1172; Bolesław I divided Silesia, Racibórz to Mieszko and Opole to Jarosław.
wars.note: The page dates the division to Bolesław's return 'at the beginning of 1173'; the Silesia page and its infobox say 1172.

wars.name: Wars of Henry the Bearded with Konrad I of Masovia
wars.outcome: War began in 1228; Konrad captured Henry at Spytkowice in 1229, beat his expedition at Gniezno in 1231 and Henry entered Kraków in 1232; the Treaty of Chełm (1233) confirmed Henry as High Duke and regent of Sandomierz and he gave up Łęczyca and Sieradz.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland and Battle of Legnica
wars.outcome: Henry II the Pious was defeated and killed at Legnica on 9 April 1241; all of Lesser Poland fell under Mongol control. Silesia kept its core; Kraków and Greater Poland were lost.
wars.note: Earlier battles at Tursko (13 February) and Tarczek and Chmielnik (18 March).

wars.name: Henry IV Probus against Bolesław II and Henry V of Legnica
wars.outcome: Henry IV was seized at Jelcz and imprisoned in 1277, his allies were beaten at Stolec on 24 April 1277, he gave Bolesław II a third of his duchy as ransom; he took Henry V of Legnica, Henry III of Głogów and Przemysł II at Sądowel in February 1281.
wars.note: Ottokar II, his ally, fell at the Marchfeld in 1278.

wars.name: War for the Kraków succession
wars.outcome: After Leszek the Black's death Henry IV Probus fought at Siewierz on 26 February 1289, took Kraków in August 1289 and held it to his death on 23 June 1290, bequeathing it to Przemysł II.

certainty.note: The Oder basin is described without boundary lines on the pages opened. The southern frontier along the Sudetes was fixed by the 1137 'boundary agreement with Bohemian duke Soběslav I' (sharp); every other frontier is a castellany limit, approximate.

sources.title: Duchy of Silesia

notes:
eu-15-e, Duchy of Silesia with the Cliopatria rows 'Duchy of Silesia' (14 shapes, 1139-1304) and 'Duchy of Wrocław' (3 shapes, 1169-1201), merged. Both rows carry Wikidata Q568638 and the Wikipedia title 'Duchy of Wrocław' is an alias: the URL Duchy_of_Breslau opens the Duchy of Silesia article (infobox 'Duchy of Silesia', 1138-1335, capital Wrocław, 'Wrocław' as the Silesian duchy's own name), and Duchy_of_Wroclaw opens 'Duke of Silesia'. One state, one dossier under the earlier slug; there is no separate duchy-of-wroc-aw dossier. The three Wrocław-row shapes, however, lie on Upper Silesia (96% inside the Upper Silesia region: Opole, Bytom, to 1176 Racibórz), not on Wrocław: they are the lands of the Silesian Piast duchies of Racibórz (Mieszko I) and Opole (Jarosław) that split off in 1172, so 1177 and 1192 are 'wrong' as Wrocław and the 1169 one is 'adjust' (Silesian to 1171). This leaves Upper Silesia 1172-1201 with no state except Cliopatria's own Duchy of Opole row (1177-1201, 6.5 thousand km2); a Duchy of Racibórz dossier for 1172-1284 is needed (Cliopatria's row starts 1285).

End: the dossier stops in 1304 with the Cliopatria row. The page runs the Wrocław duchy to 1335 (Henry VI the Good 1296-1335; 1327 treaty with John of Bohemia; Trentschin 1335; Namysłów 1348); Cliopatria shows Wrocław inside its Legnica row 1305-1313 and inside Bohemia from 1314 (gazetteer check), so the Legnica dossier should hand Wrocław back to Silesia 1305-1335 or the Silesia dossier should be extended (one new keyframe from the 1304 shape). Not done for lack of pages (Henry V the Fat, Henry VI the Good).

Cliopatria uses this row for two things. The big shapes of 1139-1146 (121.8 thousand km2) and 1236-1249 (120.1 and 110.7 thousand km2) are the realms of the High Dukes who held Silesia (Władysław II; Henry I and II): pages support Silesia plus the Seniorate (1139) and Silesia plus Lesser Poland, southwestern Greater Poland and Opole (1236); the shapes overshoot into Kuyavia, Pomerelia and Masovia. The smaller shapes are Lower Silesia with Lubusz and Głogów. Where Cliopatria gives the Seniorate to other rows (Masovia 1147-1176, Greater Poland 1177-1187 and 1227-1235, Opole 1210-1215, Sandomierz 1188-1201, 1206-1209, 1216-1226 and from 1250), the Silesian kernel is not affected.

Gaps and conflicts. (1) Silesia 1147-1162 has no territory: Bolesław IV 'took control' in 1146 and the sons returned in 1163 (Barbarossa forced Bolesław IV to cede Silesia in 1157); the dossier lets the state lapse and the Masovia row carries the land. (2) Partition dates: Silesia infobox 1172, Bolesław I page 'beginning of 1173', Duke of Silesia table 1163 (Opole-Racibórz) and 1173 (Racibórz and Opole). (3) Głogów reintegration 'c. 1185' (infobox) or 1190 (text and Bolesław I page): 1190 used. (4) Lubusz: the Silesia page says Henry 'regained' it in 1210 and held it before; the Henry I page says he took Lubusz and Gubin on 6 May 1210 and held them 'until 1218'; the 1218-1229 holder is on no page (Thuringian landgraves campaign against Lubusz from 1221); the 1248-1250 sale: Brandenburg (Silesia page) or half to the Archbishop of Magdeburg (Henry III page). Cliopatria keeps Lubusz in the outline through 1249. (5) Henry IV Probus: the Silesia page says ruler 1266-1290, the Henry IV page says adult rule from 1273 (Ottokar II 'also took over Wrocław' after Władysław's death in 1270: a Bohemian guardianship that is not carried as an event; the Bohemia dossier could record it). (6) The Cliopatria 1279 outline grows by 6.3 thousand km2 with no page; event at confidence 1. (7) Not carried because the end is undated or the extent unknown: Kalisz taken in 1284 and later traded for Ołobok, Wieluń ceded by Przemysł II in February 1281, Santok reclaimed in 1239, Kalisz given to Odonic before 1208, Henry III's help for Bolesław II in 1253, the Nysa bishopric (1290; 'Ecclesiastical Duchy of Nysa'), the 1296 partition of Henry V's heritage (Wrocław to Henry VI, Legnica to Bolesław III per the sons' list on no page opened). (8) 1297+ nothing.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Duchy of Racibórz 1172-1284 (suggested duchy-of-raciborz; the slug exists for 1285-1304 in another batch); Duchy of Legnica 1248-1278 (slug exists for 1279-1313); Duchy of Głogów 1177-1190 (slug exists for 1250-1313); Margraviate of Lusatia (Konrad II, to 1210) and the Landgraviate of Thuringia (Lubusz 1218-1230) have no dossier here. Gazetteer names needed (places): Głogów, Racibórz, Legnica, Świdnica, Środa Śląska, Strzegom, Kłodzko. Page budget: Silesia had 14 + 3 shapes (up to 9 + 2 pages); eleven pages were opened, two of them aliases (Duchy of Breslau, Duke of Silesia). [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: the region 'Lesser Poland' (four voivodeships, with Subcarpathia and Lublin to the Bug) was replaced by the Lesser Poland voivodeship (Kraków land) wherever the text says Kraków; the 1241-1242 Lubusz counterpart is Henry II's son Mieszko, not Opole.]
